# Review pack: review-data-protection

Everything a worker needs for this skill, in one file: `SKILL.md`, `references/checklist.md`, the skill's other reference files and its language-neutral standards. Language-specific standards and signals are in `packs/review-data-protection.<language>.md`. Where the instructions below say to load one of these files, use its section here instead; don't open the original. Citation columns (anchors, pages, source names) are left out: cite an element by its ID in `Finding.element` and the report script fills in `standard` and `url`. `sources.md` is maintainer material and is not included.

## File: `SKILL.md`

### Review: Data Protection

Assesses the engineering controls a codebase uses to protect personal data, using local, pinned summaries of
OWASP, NIST, GDPR principle text, RFC 2606 and vendor guidance. The reviewer judges only what the code and
configuration show. It never judges lawful basis, consent records, privacy notices or DPIAs, and the report never
states that a target complies (or fails to comply) with GDPR, CCPA or any other law.

#### Inputs

Entity and model classes, DTOs and serializers, controllers that return data, client-side storage and cookie code,
third-party SDK setup (error trackers, analytics, LLM/AI and email/SMS clients), fixtures, seed and sample data,
migrations, classification and redaction setup, and deletion, retention or data-copy code, per `compliance-inventory`.
The dispatch payload may also carry `piiCandidates` (file, line, rule, confidence; never the value) found by the
step-01 pattern pass in test, fixture, seed and sample files, and `personalDataSignals` (why the subject applies).

#### Standards (local, authoritative)

- `references/standards/owasp-data-protection.md` — CSD-01…05, A04-01…05, BOP-01…04, UPP-01…02, HSP-01…03,
  QSE-01. Always load.
- `references/standards/nist-sp-800-122.md` — SP122-01…09. Always load.
- `references/standards/gdpr-principles.md` — GDPR-01…05 (principle summaries). Always load.
- `references/standards/rfc-2606-reserved-names.md` — RSV-01. Always load.
- `references/standards/third-party-sdks.md` — TPS-01…05 (Sentry per platform, Application Insights). Always load;
  each row applies only when that SDK is in the files.
- `references/standards/dotnet-data-protection.md` — DND-01…02. Load when language `csharp` is detected.
- `references/standards/java-data-protection.md` — JVD-01…02. Load when language `java` is detected.
- `references/standards/python-data-protection.md` — PYD-01…02. Load when language `python` is detected.
- Do **not** fetch any URL for this skill, and never use remembered SDK or framework defaults: a default counts only
  when a localized element states it. Do not load `references/standards/MAINTENANCE.md`.
- If no element covers a situation: apply the closest element if it clearly fits; otherwise mark the check N/A
  ("not covered by localized standard") and add `localized-standard-gap: <description>` to `notes`.

#### Procedure

1. Load `references/checklist.md`, `references/sources.md`, the standards files that apply (above), and
   `references/languages/<id>.md` for each detected language (detection signals only; they cite no standard).
2. Find the personal data first: entity, model and DTO fields named like the identifiers in SP122-02 (name, email,
   phone, address, date of birth, national or tax ID, passport, card or account number, IP address, biometrics),
   classification attributes, and user or customer tables in migrations. Then follow those fields to storage,
   API responses, URLs and client storage, third-party SDK calls, fixtures and deletion code.
3. **Candidates.** When the payload has `piiCandidates`, read each candidate line with ±3 lines of context, even when
   the file isn't in your own list. Decide whether the value is real-looking personal data or clearly synthetic
   (reserved domains per RSV-01, published test card numbers, obviously fake values). Real-looking values fail
   DPR-05 with `confidence: high` for a Luhn-valid card number or a checksum-valid IBAN that the context confirms,
   `medium` otherwise. When `piiCandidatesTotal` is larger than the list, add
   `pii-candidates-truncated: <total>` to `notes`.
4. For each check DPR-01…DPR-08, evaluate the elements it lists against the subject's files. Mark a check N/A with a
   reason when no element applies (e.g. DPR-03 when there is no URL, client storage or cookie code; DPR-07 when there
   are no data-copy scripts; DPR-04 when no third-party SDK or outbound personal-data call is in the files).
5. Evidence rules: fail an element only on concrete code or configuration in the files (see the evidence notes in
   `checklist.md`). A missing control counts only where the files show the personal data it should protect. Don't
   fail on speculation, and use confidence `medium` unless the evidence is unambiguous.
6. **Ownership** (Boundaries). These stay with their own subjects; don't report them here:
   - personal data or secrets in logs and error reports: `review-security-operational` SEC-OP-03;
   - personal data in telemetry attributes and baggage: `review-observability` OBS-10;
   - `Cache-Control: no-store` on sensitive responses: `review-security-web-api` SEC-WA-08;
   - credentials (passwords, tokens, API keys) in URLs: `review-security-web-api` SEC-WA-10;
   - mass assignment and over-posting on input: `review-security-input-injection` SEC-II-01;
   - tokens in `localStorage`/`sessionStorage`, session cookies, password hashing: `review-security-identity-access`;
   - TLS and HSTS in transit: `review-security-web-api`; hardcoded keys and secrets: SEC-OP-05.

   DPR-02 owns over-exposure on output (responses and serializers). DPR-03 owns personal data other than credentials
   in URLs, query strings and client storage. Store-level encryption in IaC is judged under DPR-01 only when the
   payload says `advanced: true` and IaC files are in your list; otherwise judge field- and application-level
   controls only.
7. Severity: every Finding takes its check's default severity from `checklist.md`. When several elements fail on the
   same evidence, write one finding.
8. Citations: set `element` to the failed element's ID (e.g. `BOP-03`); the report script derives `standard` and
   `url`. Prefer a vendor element (DND/JVD/PYD/TPS), then an OWASP element, then NIST, then GDPR. Cite a GDPR element
   only when nothing more specific fits, and word the finding as an engineering gap ("personal data is returned
   that the endpoint doesn't need"), never as a legal conclusion.
9. **Redaction.** Evidence excerpts never contain the personal data or secret itself: replace the value with
   `<redacted:kind>` (e.g. `"cardNumber": "<redacted:card-number>"`), keeping the field name and the line numbers.
10. If the reference date (date part of `startedAt`) is more than 9 months after a standards file's "Localized"
    date, add `localized-standard-stale: <file> localized <date>` to `notes`.

#### Output

Findings, strengths and check results per `compliance-review-core`'s `finding-schema.md`.

### Checklist — Data Protection

Subject: Data Protection

Each check is evaluated through the elements it lists; every element belongs to exactly one check. Element
definitions, anchors and citation bases are in `standards/`. Every Finding takes its check's default severity
(`../SKILL.md` step 7). These are engineering controls only: no check judges lawful basis, consent or legal
compliance.

| id | Sub-subject | Check | Default severity | Elements | Source |
|----|-------------|-------|------------------|----------|--------|
| DPR-01 | Storage | Sensitive personal fields (national IDs, payment card numbers, health and biometric data) are minimized and encrypted, tokenized or hashed at rest at field or store level, with sound algorithms and keys kept apart from the data; no plaintext card numbers | Error | CSD-01, CSD-02, CSD-03, CSD-04, A04-03, A04-04, A04-05, UPP-01, SP122-09, GDPR-05 | CSD, A04, UPP, SP122, GDPR |
| DPR-02 | Exposure | API responses and serializers expose only the properties the caller needs: DTOs, projections or explicit field lists instead of persistence entities, with sensitive fields excluded | Error | BOP-01, BOP-02, BOP-03, BOP-04, SP122-03, SP122-08, GDPR-04, JVD-01, JVD-02, PYD-01, PYD-02 | BOP, SP122, GDPR, JVD, PYD |
| DPR-03 | Exposure | Personal data isn't put in URLs or query strings, `localStorage`/`sessionStorage` or IndexedDB, and sensitive form fields don't invite autofill | Warning | CSD-05, HSP-01, HSP-02, HSP-03, QSE-01, TPS-05 | CSD, HSP, QSE, TPS |
| DPR-04 | Sharing | Personal data sent to third parties (error trackers, analytics, LLM/AI APIs, email/SMS providers, embedded third-party content) is minimized or scrubbed; SDK switches that send user data by default are turned off or restricted | Warning | UPP-02, GDPR-01, TPS-01, TPS-02, TPS-03, TPS-04 | UPP, GDPR, TPS |
| DPR-05 | Non-Production Data | Test fixtures, seed data and samples use synthetic data (reserved domains such as `example.com`, published test card numbers, obviously fake values), not real-looking personal data | Warning | SP122-06, RSV-01 | SP122, RSV |
| DPR-06 | Lifecycle | Personal data has a deletion or anonymization path, and retention is bounded where the code stores it (delete or erase operations, purge jobs, TTLs) | Information | SP122-04, GDPR-02 | SP122, GDPR |
| DPR-07 | Non-Production Data | Scripts and jobs that copy production data to other environments mask, pseudonymize or anonymize personal fields, keeping any re-identification key apart | Warning | SP122-05, SP122-07, GDPR-03 | SP122, GDPR |
| DPR-08 | Governance | Personal-data fields are identified in code (classification attributes or annotations, or a documented data inventory) and classified data gets the controls its class requires | Information | A04-01, A04-02, SP122-01, SP122-02, DND-01, DND-02 | A04, SP122, DND |

Totals: 20 OWASP + 9 NIST + 5 GDPR + 1 RFC 2606 + 5 third-party SDK + 2 DND + 2 JVD + 2 PYD = 46 elements across 8 checks.

#### Evidence notes

- **Personal data** means the identifiers and linked data listed in SP122-02. "Sensitive personal data" (DPR-01) is the
  subset whose exposure causes the most harm: national and tax IDs, passport and driver's licence numbers, payment
  card and bank account numbers, health, biometric and precise location data.
- **DPR-01:** fail when an entity, table or document stores sensitive personal data in a plain column with no field
  encryption, value converter, tokenization, hashing or truncation in the files; when full card numbers or CVV are
  stored at all; or when application-level encryption uses ECB, a custom scheme or keys stored beside the data. Store-
  level encryption shown in IaC passes for the store it covers (advanced usage only). Names, emails and phone numbers
  alone don't fail DPR-01.
- **DPR-02:** fail when a controller, route handler, resolver or MCP tool returns a persistence entity or ORM model
  that has personal or internal fields the endpoint doesn't need (password hashes, other users' contact data, internal
  flags), returns `to_json()`/`model_dump()`/`__dict__` of such an object, or when a serializer exposes every model
  field (`fields = '__all__'`, no `@JsonIgnore` on sensitive properties). Input binding (over-posting) is SEC-II-01.
- **DPR-03:** fail on routes, links, redirects or client calls that put personal data (email, phone, name, national
  ID, date of birth) in the path or query string; on `localStorage`/`sessionStorage`/IndexedDB writes of personal
  data; and, as a lower-confidence finding, on sensitive personal input fields without `autocomplete="off"`.
  Credentials and tokens are not judged here.
- **DPR-04:** fail when an error-tracker or analytics SDK is configured to send user data (`SendDefaultPii = true`,
  Sentry `userInfo`/`user_info` left at its default where the files set user identity, request bodies or local
  variables collected on endpoints that handle personal data), or when code sends personal data to an LLM/AI,
  email or SMS API without minimizing it to what the call needs. Telemetry attributes are OBS-10.
- **DPR-05:** fail on real-looking personal data in test, fixture, seed or sample files: Luhn-valid card numbers that
  aren't published test numbers, national-ID shapes, checksum-valid IBANs or emails on non-reserved domains attached
  to person names. Use the payload's `piiCandidates` as a starting point (SKILL.md step 3).
- **DPR-06:** fail (Information) when the files store personal data and show no delete, erase, anonymize or purge
  path for it and no TTL or retention setting. Soft-delete flags that never purge count as no deletion path.
- **DPR-07:** fail when a script or job copies a production database (dump, restore, bacpac, snapshot) into another
  environment without a masking or anonymizing step in the files. N/A when no such script exists.
- **DPR-08:** fail (Information) when the files hold personal data and nothing identifies it (no classification
  attributes, annotations or data inventory document), or when fields are labelled sensitive but handled like any
  other field.

## File: `references/standards/owasp-data-protection.md`

*Load rule: CSD-01…05, A04-01…05, BOP-01…04, UPP-01…02, HSP-01…03, QSE-01. Always load.*

### OWASP data-protection guidance — localized summary

- Level: `MUST` where the source says must/must not/never/do not/always, gives an unqualified imperative, or is a
  Top 10 "How to prevent" bullet; `SHOULD` for should/recommended/"consider"/"advised"; `REVIEW` for a "Description"
  or "Is the API vulnerable?" weakness (treated like `MUST`). Levels are informational: every Finding takes its
  check's default severity (`../../SKILL.md` step 7).
- Scope: the sections listed in the anchors only. The Mass Assignment Cheat Sheet and API3's mass-assignment bullets
  belong to `review-security-input-injection` (SEC-II-01) and are not localized here; key hard-coding belongs to
  SEC-OP-05; local-storage tokens and session IDs belong to `review-security-identity-access`.

#### Cryptographic Storage Cheat Sheet (CSD)

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Code/config evidence | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CSD-01 | SHOULD | Avoid storing sensitive information wherever possible; the best protection is not to store it (card details especially). | full card numbers, CVV or national IDs stored without a business need | DPR-01 |
| CSD-02 | SHOULD | Choose the encryption layer (application, database, filesystem, hardware) from the threat model; disk or hardware encryption doesn't protect against a remote compromise of the server. | sensitive columns stored in plaintext, protected only by disk or volume encryption | DPR-01 |
| CSD-03 | SHOULD | Application-level encryption uses AES (≥ 128-bit, ideally 256-bit) in an authenticated mode (GCM/CCM) from a maintained library; CTR/CBC only with separate authentication (Encrypt-then-MAC); no ECB, no custom algorithms; RSA ≥ 2048 bits with OAEP padding. | `CipherMode.ECB`, `AES/ECB/…`, `Cipher.getInstance("AES")`, home-made XOR or Base64 "encryption", RSA without OAEP | DPR-01 |
| CSD-04 | SHOULD | Keys that encrypt stored data are kept apart from the data (not in the same database), are themselves encrypted by a separate key-encryption key where possible (envelope encryption), and use the platform's key vault, HSM or OS-protected storage where available. | encryption key stored in a table or column next to the ciphertext; key read from the same database it protects | DPR-01 |
| CSD-05 | SHOULD | Encrypted data is still protected by access control; the application doesn't rely on encrypted URL parameters to protect information. | encrypted or encoded personal data in query strings treated as the protection | DPR-03 |

#### Top 10:2025 A04 Cryptographic Failures (A04)

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Code/config evidence | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A04-01 | MUST | Classify and label the data the application processes, stores or transmits; identify which data is sensitive under privacy laws, regulations or business needs. | entities holding personal data with no classification attribute, annotation or data inventory | DPR-08 |
| A04-02 | MUST | Apply the security controls each data classification requires. | fields labelled sensitive but stored, returned or shared like any other field | DPR-08 |
| A04-03 | MUST | Don't store sensitive data unnecessarily: discard it as soon as possible, or use PCI DSS compliant tokenization or truncation. | full PAN or CVV columns; card data kept after the payment completes | DPR-01 |
| A04-04 | MUST | Encrypt all sensitive data at rest. | plaintext national-ID, health or card columns with no field encryption, converter or tokenization | DPR-01 |
| A04-05 | MUST | Use well-trusted implementations, authenticated encryption and current algorithms with proper key management; avoid deprecated functions, modes and padding (MD5, SHA-1, CBC, PKCS #1 v1.5) for protecting data. | `MD5`/`SHA1` used to "protect" personal fields; unauthenticated CBC; PKCS #1 v1.5 encryption | DPR-01 |

#### API Security Top 10:2023 API3 Broken Object Property Level Authorization (BOP)

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Code/config evidence | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BOP-01 | REVIEW | An endpoint is vulnerable when it exposes object properties that are sensitive and shouldn't be read by the caller (formerly "Excessive Data Exposure"). | responses carrying password hashes, internal flags, other users' contact or location data | DPR-02 |
| BOP-02 | MUST | When exposing an object through an endpoint, make sure the caller should have access to every property returned. | one entity returned to every role, with no per-caller shaping | DPR-02 |
| BOP-03 | MUST | Avoid generic serialization of whole objects (`to_json()`, `to_string()`); cherry-pick the properties to return. | controller returns the ORM entity; `jsonify(user.__dict__)`; `return Ok(dbContext.Users.ToList())` | DPR-02 |
| BOP-04 | SHOULD | Keep returned data structures to the minimum the endpoint's business requirements need, and define and enforce the data returned (schema-based response validation). | list endpoints returning full records; no response models or schemas | DPR-02 |

#### User Privacy Protection Cheat Sheet (UPP)

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Code/config evidence | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| UPP-01 | MUST | Private user data is encrypted in storage, with keys of sufficient length under strict technical and procedural access conditions. (Credential hashing is judged by identity-access.) | private messages, documents or personal profiles stored in plaintext | DPR-01 |
| UPP-02 | SHOULD | Applications that embed external third-party content (avatars, signatures, photo attachments, images in HTML email) consider letting users block it, so a third party can't learn users' IP addresses. | user-supplied external image URLs rendered directly in feeds or messages, with no proxy or block option | DPR-04 |

#### HTML5 Security Cheat Sheet — storage and PII input hints (HSP)

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Code/config evidence | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HSP-01 | SHOULD | Don't store sensitive information in `localStorage` (any XSS can read it all); use `sessionStorage` when persistence isn't needed. | `localStorage.setItem('user', JSON.stringify(profile))` with email, phone or address | DPR-03 |
| HSP-02 | SHOULD | Don't assume IndexedDB provides confidentiality; avoid storing sensitive data there, or design encryption and key management for device access. | personal records cached in IndexedDB in plaintext | DPR-03 |
| HSP-03 | SHOULD | Sensitive personal input fields where autofill is inappropriate carry `autocomplete="off"`; it is a hint, not a no-storage guarantee. | national-ID or card inputs without `autocomplete="off"` | DPR-03 |

#### Information exposure through query strings in URL (QSE)

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Code/config evidence | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QSE-01 | REVIEW | Sensitive data, including personal data such as email addresses, isn't passed in URL query strings: it leaks through Referer headers, web logs, shared systems, browser history and caches, and third-party monitoring, even over HTTPS. | `GET /users?email=…`, `[FromQuery] string email`, links or redirects that carry email, phone or ID values | DPR-03 |

## File: `references/standards/nist-sp-800-122.md`

*Load rule: SP122-01…09. Always load.*

### NIST SP 800-122 — Guide to Protecting the Confidentiality of PII — localized summary

- Level: the source's own keyword (`SHOULD`, `MUST` for "required") where the summarized sentence has one, otherwise
  `REVIEW`. Levels are informational: every Finding takes its check's default severity.
- Terminology mapping: "organization" = the team that owns the target; "agency" rules (Privacy Act, NARA schedules,
  OMB memoranda) are not localized. Only engineering safeguards that can be seen in code are summarized.
- Section: primary section first; put it in `Finding.notes` when citing.

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Applies when | Check | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SP122-01 | MUST | Identify all PII the system holds, including PII handled for it by third parties, using documentation, data inventories or automated discovery. | personal data in the files | DPR-08 | §2.1 |
| SP122-02 | REVIEW | PII is information that distinguishes or traces a person (name; SSN, passport, driver's licence, taxpayer, patient, financial account and card numbers; street and email address; IP or MAC address linked to a person; telephone numbers; photos and biometric data; vehicle registration) plus linked or linkable medical, educational, financial and employment data. | always (definition for every check) | DPR-08 | §2.1, §2.2 |
| SP122-03 | SHOULD | Limit the PII used and collected to the minimum necessary for the authorized purpose; PII that serves no current business purpose is no longer used or collected. | personal fields collected or returned | DPR-02 | §4.2.1 |
| SP122-04 | SHOULD | Regularly review PII holdings and properly destroy PII that is no longer relevant and necessary. | personal data stored | DPR-06 | §4.2.1 |
| SP122-05 | SHOULD | De-identified records use a re-identification code or pseudonym not derived from other information about the person, and the means of re-identification is kept in a separate system with access controls. | pseudonymization or masking code | DPR-07 | §4.2.3 |
| SP122-06 | REVIEW | Test systems use anonymized substitutes (synthetic data derived from anonymized PII) instead of PII, so test data is no longer PII. | fixtures, seed or sample data | DPR-05 | §4.2.4 |
| SP122-07 | MUST | PII used in a test environment is protected at the same level as in production. | production data copied to other environments | DPR-07 | §4.2.4 |
| SP122-08 | REVIEW | Least privilege and access enforcement for PII: users and processes reach only the PII fields their role needs, preferably through an application that restricts the fields instead of direct access to the data store. | endpoints or queries returning personal data | DPR-02 | §4.3 (AC-3, AC-6) |
| SP122-09 | REVIEW | Protect PII at rest, usually by encrypting the stored information (SC-28), including backups and removable media. | personal data stored | DPR-01 | §4.3 (SC-28) |

## File: `references/standards/gdpr-principles.md`

*Load rule: GDPR-01…05 (principle summaries). Always load.*

### GDPR — data-protection principles (engineering summary) — localized summary

- Scope: **principle summaries only**, for engineering controls that can be seen in code: Art. 5(1)(c) data
  minimisation, Art. 5(1)(e) storage limitation, Art. 25 data protection by design and by default, Art. 32(1)(a)
  pseudonymisation and encryption. Lawful basis, consent, transparency, data-subject rights procedures, DPIAs and
  accountability are not localized and are never judged. A finding never states that the target complies or doesn't
  comply with the Regulation.
- Level: `MUST` ("shall"). Levels are informational: every Finding takes its check's default severity.

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Applies when | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GDPR-01 | MUST | (Art. 5(1)(c)) Data minimisation: personal data are adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary for the purpose; for engineering, send third parties only the personal fields the call needs. | personal data sent to SDKs or external APIs | DPR-04 |
| GDPR-02 | MUST | (Art. 5(1)(e)) Storage limitation: personal data are kept in a form that identifies people for no longer than necessary for the purpose. | personal data stored | DPR-06 |
| GDPR-03 | MUST | (Art. 25(1)) Data protection by design: technical measures such as pseudonymisation implement the data-protection principles, such as data minimisation, in an effective manner. | pseudonymization, masking or data-copy code | DPR-07 |
| GDPR-04 | MUST | (Art. 25(2)) Data protection by default: by default only the personal data necessary for each specific purpose are processed (amount collected, extent of processing, storage period, accessibility), and personal data aren't made accessible to an indefinite number of people without the person's intervention. | personal data returned or published | DPR-02 |
| GDPR-05 | MUST | (Art. 32(1)(a)) Security of processing: appropriate technical measures, including the pseudonymisation and encryption of personal data, give a level of security appropriate to the risk. | personal data stored | DPR-01 |

## File: `references/standards/third-party-sdks.md`

*Load rule: TPS-01…05 (Sentry per platform, Application Insights). Always load; each row applies only when that SDK is in the files.*

### Third-party SDK data collection (error trackers, APM) — localized summary

- Applies only when the SDK is in the files: Sentry rows by platform (`Sentry` NuGet package / `io.sentry` / `sentry-sdk`
  / `@sentry/*`), Application Insights when its SDK or the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry distro is referenced. Language
  detection doesn't gate these rows.
- Level: `MUST` for "do not" guidance; **(Default)** marks an element that states SDK behaviour or a default. Defaults
  stated here are the only SDK defaults a worker may rely on. Levels are informational: every Finding takes its
  check's default severity.
- Ownership: telemetry attributes and custom telemetry content belong to `review-observability` (OBS-10); these rows
  judge only the SDK switches that send user data, and URLs.

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Code/config evidence | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TPS-01 | SHOULD | **(Default)** Sentry .NET: `SendDefaultPii` is off by default. When `true`, the SDK sends cookies, logged-in user information (email, user ID, username), the user's IP address, the full absolute request URI and the machine name. The request query string is always sent. | `o.SendDefaultPii = true`; `"SendDefaultPii": true` in `appsettings*.json` | DPR-04 |
| TPS-02 | SHOULD | **(Default)** Sentry Java: `dataCollection.userInfo` defaults to `true`, adding user identity (including Spring Security usernames) and the user's IP address; headers, cookies and query parameters use deny-lists by default; Spring MVC request bodies are collected only once `maxRequestBodySize` is set (default `NONE`). | no `dataCollection.userInfo=false` where personal data flows; `maxRequestBodySize` raised on personal-data endpoints | DPR-04 |
| TPS-03 | SHOULD | **(Default)** Sentry Python (SDK 3.x): `data_collection.user_info` defaults to `True` (user id, email, username, IP address); request headers, cookies and query parameters are sent with deny-list scrubbing; JSON and form request bodies, local variables in stack frames (not scrubbed by default) and gen-AI inputs and outputs are collected by default. | `sentry_sdk.init(...)` with no `data_collection` limits (`user_info`, `http_bodies`, `stack_frame_variables`, `gen_ai`) in an app that handles personal data | DPR-04 |
| TPS-04 | SHOULD | **(Default)** Sentry JavaScript: the user's IP address is sent by default (`dataCollection.userInfo`); on the server, incoming-request cookies and the full query string are collected by default (values of sensitive keys filtered); data set with `Sentry.setUser()` is always sent. | `Sentry.init` without `dataCollection` limits; `Sentry.setUser({ email, … })` | DPR-04 |
| TPS-05 | MUST | Application Insights: don't put sensitive data in URLs (request URLs are collected as telemetry). | personal data in routes or query strings of an app instrumented with Application Insights | DPR-03 |
